rationale:
FIXES A DEFECT IN THE WRITE-TIME CITATION PROBE THAT MISLED ME INTO ASSERTING A FALSE PRODUCTION DANGER IN FOUR DOCUMENTS AND A LANDMINE.

RUNBOOK_lendzy §8 step 4 tells every register author to verify a candidate quote with `cmd/fcaquotecheck`, and §8g states the rule it exists to serve: 'never validate a citation host with an instrument other than the one that will re-check it daily.' §8 describes the tool as calling 'the production fetch + extraction'. IT CALLED THE PRODUCTION EXTRACTION ONLY — it did its own bare http.Get and ran VisibleTextFromHTML over whatever bytes came back, with none of fetchCitationDocument's gates (scheme check, timeout, non-200, CONTENT TYPE, bot-challenge detection).

WHAT THAT COST, measured 2026-09-03 against the CMA draft substantive Order: the probe returned HTTP 200, 392,144 raw bytes, 296,699 characters of extracted binary noise, and `false` for every quote INCLUDING 'Compliance Date' which is certainly in the document, AND `false` for the deliberately-absent control. Two falses means the instrument is blind; it reads exactly like a mistyped quote. I then inferred a PRODUCTION drift danger from that blind probe and wrote it into a LANDMINE, migration 759's header, this lane's NOTES, the vetcomparison lane's NOTES and the owner's prose log: 'a citation there would read as citation_lost drift every day, for ever.'

THAT CLAIM IS FALSE AND PRODUCTION WAS NEVER AT RISK. refreshCitationFact -> verifyCitationLiveForRule -> fetchCitationDocument, and that fetch refuses a non-html/xml/text content type at evidence_citations.go:143-148, returning an error that classifies as `fetch_error` -> outcome `error`. The file's own header has said so all along: 'fetch failed (network, 403, 5xx, unsupported content type) -> UNKNOWN, not drift ... Reported as an error, never as loss', and 'PDFs and other non-text content are refused rather than half-read'. I never read it. All five documents are being corrected in the same sweep as this change.

THE FIX IS ONE EXPORT, NOT A SECOND IMPLEMENTATION. A mirror that drifts from production is the exact failure this package warns about twice in comments, and re-implementing the gates in the probe would rebuild the defect one layer along. So fetchCitationDocument gains an exported wrapper and the probe calls it.

plan.summary: Adds FetchCitationDocumentForProbe, an exported wrapper over the unexported fetchCitationDocument, and rewrites cmd/fcaquotecheck to call it instead of doing its own http.Get. The probe now surfaces an unsupported content type, a non-200, a bot-challenge interstitial and a UA-differential blank AT WRITE TIME, in production's own words, and tells the author what to do instead (cite an HTML source, or keep the citation with reverifiable:false + staleness_days). It also warns explicitly when EVERY quote including the control returns false — the signature of a blind instrument.
plan.risks:
1. NO PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR CHANGES. The wrapper delegates; fetchCitationDocument, verifyCitationLive(ForRule) and refreshCitationFact are untouched. The only caller of the new symbol is a cmd/ probe. Verified by build: `go build ./cmd/fcaquotecheck/ ./platform/orchestration/actions/`.
2. IT WIDENS THE PACKAGE'S EXPORTED SURFACE BY ONE FUNCTION. The alternative — mirroring the gates in the probe — is worse and is the defect being fixed. The export is named ...ForProbe and its doc comment states it is a test/probe seam, so a future reader is not invited to build production paths on it.
3. THE PROBE NOW EXITS 1 ON AN UNFETCHABLE SOURCE where it previously exited 0 with a row of `false`. Anything scripted around it that keyed on exit status will now see a failure — which is the correct signal and was previously indistinguishable from 'quote not found'. No script in the repo calls it (grep: the tool is invoked by hand from RUNBOOK §8 step 4).
4. The RUNBOOK's own §8/§8g wording ('calls the production fetch + extraction') becomes TRUE with this change rather than aspirational. It is being corrected in the same sweep to say what it now does and to name the two-falses tell.

edits.rationale: Export the production fetch as a named probe seam, with a comment recording exactly which defect this closes and why a mirror was refused.
Call the production fetch; report an unfetchable source as production would; tell the author the supported alternative; and name the two-falses tell.

grounded_in: evidence_citations.go:143-148 — `ctype := strings.ToLower(resp.Header.Get("Content-Type"))` … `if ctype != "" && !isHTML && !isText { return "", fmt.Errorf("unsupported content type %q — mark the fact reverifiable:false and attest it by hand", ctype) }`.

evidence_citations.go header, verbatim: 'fetch failed (network, 403, 5xx, unsupported content type) → UNKNOWN, not drift. A paywall going up is not evidence the fact is wrong; it is evidence we can no longer check. Reported as an error, never as loss.' and 'PDFs and other non-text content are refused rather than half-read: a fact whose source the platform cannot re-fetch as text should carry "reverifiable": false and a human attestation of having read it.'

refresh_evidence_base_action.go:919-931 refreshCitationFact doc comment: 'error — the source could not be checked (network, 403, PDF). Unknown is not loss: reported, never treated as drift.' and the switch at :972-977 routing FailClass=='fetch_error' to Outcome 'error'.

verifyCitationLiveForRule:86 `text, err := fetchCitationDocument(ctx, cit.URL)` then `if err != nil { return citationVerifyOutcome{FailClass: "fetch_error", ...} }` — the chain that makes a PDF an error rather than drift.

RUNBOOK_lendzy §8g: 'The one control that catches all three is §8 step 4: the write-time probe THROUGH the production matcher (cmd/fcaquotecheck calls the production fetch + extraction) … Never validate a citation host with an instrument other than the one that will re-check it daily.' — the rule the old probe broke while being cited as its exemplar.

Measured 2026-09-03, old probe vs the CMA draft Order: `HTTP 200 raw=392144 visible=296699`, false for 'means a Veterinary Business with 15 or more', false for 'Compliance Date', false for the absent control. Measured 2026-09-04, new probe, same URL: 'NOT VERIFIABLE UNATTENDED: unsupported content type "application/pdf"'. Control that the probe still works: gov.uk AHC page returns visible=5886, true for '10 days for entry into the EU', false for the absent control.
